messages:
maria (support): Luis from Acme reports that their embeddings are coming back different sizes depending on which deployment they hit. Hosted -> 1536, Dedicated -> 768. Customer is seeing index mismatches downstream. Can we triage? :frowning:

luis (customer): Correct. When we call the hosted endpoint we get arrays of length 1536; when we route to our dedicated pool we get 768. We pinned to `open-embed-3` in our code. This started after yesterday's dedicated rollout.

maria (support): Thanks. Can you paste a minimal curl you used and a tiny sample response (headers + first few values)? No secrets, redact api_key.

luis (customer): Sure — here's a repro (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embedding-3","input":"dog"}'
```
Response hosted (trace):
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.12, ... 1536 values total]}],"model":"open-embedding-3-large","usage":{}}
```
When we hit dedicated by using the `x-deployment: dedicated` header (their client adds this):
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.02, -0.004, ... 768 values total]}],"model":"open-embedding-3-base","usage":{}}
```

maria (support): Ok that's useful. Eli / Zack, looks like model variant mismatch — hosted returning `-large` (1536) and dedicated returning `-base` (768). Could be catalog mapping or a pinning problem in the dedicated model pool. Any recent changes? :eyes:

eli (eng-ml): I saw a deploy yesterday that added fallback mappings for older dedicated pools. The mapping logic will choose the nearest compatible variant if the exact model isn't available. But it should honor a full model id if provided. Their requests use `open-embedding-3` (alias) not the full variant name, so the dedicated pool's catalog appears to resolve to `open-embedding-3-base`.

zack (dedicated-ops): Confirmed. Dedicated pool 7 has only `open-embedding-3-base` in the local catalog because the larger variant hadn't been synced to that region due to a sync failure during the rollout. Sync error was flagged by deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: sync failed - catalog-sync/7 - quota-exceeded` around 2026-03-10T22:03Z. I raised a patch but didn't complete the downstream roll.

maria (support): So root cause seems to be: customer used a short alias, different deployment catalogs resolved alias to different variants -> dim mismatch. Is that the short explanation we can give the customer?

eli (eng-ml): Yes. Quick triage checklist: 1) Confirm model variant resolution (call GET /v1/models/open-embedding-3 or inspect `x-model-variant` header returned) 2) If dedicated catalog doesn't have large variant, sync/upload it 3) Customer can temporarily force the full variant name `open-embedding-3-large` in payload to ensure parity. 4) Add parity test (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to CI.

maria (support): Luis — can you try specifying `open-embedding-3-large` explicitly and tell us if both endpoints return 1536? If yes, we can advise a temporary workaround while we sync your dedicated pool.

luis (customer): Trying now...

luis (customer): Quick check: when I pass "model":"open-embedding-3-large" dedicated returns 404: `model not found`. Hosted returns 1536 as before. So dedicated pool literally doesn't have the large variant.

zack (dedicated-ops): That matches our logs — large variant not present. I'll queue a catalog sync to pool 7 now. ETA ~10m. I will post progress here.

deploy-bot: catalog-sync started for pool 7 (job id cs-9812).

eli (eng-ml): While Zack runs the sync, a note: batching / caching won't change embedding dimensionality. If anyone suspects truncation from batching we can rule it out quickly by looking at response shapes in raw logs — these show full vectors of different lengths, so it's clearly variant mismatch. Also check the `x-model-variant` header we added to embeddings responses — that'll be the quickest verification.

maria (support): Also checking billing corner-case: if a customer switches between variants sizes we bill per-token/unit differently. Need to flag billing so they don't get surprised. @finance FYI (we'll CC afterwards).

zack (dedicated-ops): catalog-sync completed, jobs: cs-9812 -> success. Large variant uploaded to pool 7.

deploy-bot: catalog-sync success for pool 7 (cs-9812).

luis (customer): Re-tested by forcing full name — dedicated now accepts `open-embedding-3-large` and returns 1536. Great.

maria (support): Excellent. I'll relay that and propose a permanent fix. Proposed remediation plan: 1) Sync missing variants to all dedicated/private pools (zack to run sweep + monitor) 2) Change alias resolution: prefer the highest-dim variant only if that's what hosted resolves to, or require exact alias-to-variant mapping in the catalog (eli to propose) 3) Add a parity CI test that issues embeddings to hosted+dedi+private for a set of aliases and asserts identical `embedding_size` and `x-model-variant` (eng-ml + eng-sre) 4) Add user-facing guidance recommending customers pin to explicit variant for storage/indexing-critical flows 5) Notify billing if there's a size+price delta and consider a onetime credit for Acme since they ingested mixed dims and had index errors.

eli (eng-ml): I'll open an RFC for alias resolution change and add the CI job as a failing test for the release branch.

zack (dedicated-ops): I'll kick off the global sync sweep, start with pools that had recent rollouts. Will post metrics when finished.

maria (support): Luis, do you want us to backfill a corrected set of embeddings for the documents that were indexed with the wrong dim? We can offer a one-time backfill script (we'd need a short maintenance window if your index needs re-ingesting).

luis (customer): Yes please — we lost some re-rank accuracy. A backfill would be appreciated. We'll coordinate a midday window tomorrow.

maria (support): Noted. I'll schedule and loop in solutions. Final customer-facing summary (draft): "We found that the dedicated pool did not have the larger embedding variant synced, so when you used the alias `open-embedding-3` different deployments resolved to different variants (1536 vs 768). We synced the missing variant; to avoid this in future please either pin the explicit variant `open-embedding-3-large` or we will update our alias resolution/CI parity to guarantee consistent resolution across hosted/dedicated/private. We're offering a backfill to re-ingest vectors indexed with the wrong size." Any edits?

eli (eng-ml): Fine. Add line: "We will add an automated parity check to detect catalog drift and alert ops".

maria (support): Added. I'll send to Luis and set the backfill appointment. Marking thread resolved once backfill scheduled. :white_check_mark:
